s.note: Soft baked buns filled with buttery cabbage, onion, egg and dill
s.how: Mix 500g plain flour, 7g dried yeast, 1 tbsp caster sugar and 1 tsp salt with 250ml warm milk, 60g melted butter and 1 egg, and knead for 10 minutes until smooth. Cover and prove for an hour until doubled. Meanwhile boil 2 eggs for 9 minutes, and cook 500g finely shredded white cabbage and 1 diced onion slowly in 40g butter for 25 minutes until soft and sweet. Season with 0.5 tsp salt and 0.5 tsp pepper, cool, then mix in the chopped eggs and 2 tbsp chopped dill. Divide the dough into 16, flatten each, fill, pinch closed and set seam side down on lined trays. Rest 15 minutes, brush with beaten egg and bake at 200C for 18 minutes until golden.

s.note: Crisp spiced onion fritters in chickpea batter with mint and coriander yoghurt
s.how: Toss 3 thinly sliced onions with 1 tsp salt and leave 10 minutes. Stir in 150g chickpea flour, 2 tbsp rice flour, 1 tsp each of ground cumin, turmeric and chilli powder, 1 chopped green chilli and half a cup of chopped coriander, then add about 100ml water to make a thick, sticky batter. Blend 200g Greek yoghurt with half a cup each of mint and coriander leaves and the juice of a lime. Heat 1 litre vegetable oil to 175C and fry heaped spoonfuls in batches for 4 to 5 minutes until deep golden and crisp. Drain and serve hot with the yoghurt.

m.note: Emirati spiced rice with slow-cooked lamb, dried lime, cardamom and tomato, topped with fried onion, sultanas and almonds
m.how: Rinse 400g basmati rice and leave it to soak. Brown 1kg boneless lamb shoulder in 5cm pieces in 2 tbsp vegetable oil, then add 2 sliced onions and cook for 10 minutes until soft. Stir in 4 crushed garlic cloves, 1 tbsp grated ginger, 2 tsp each of ground cumin and coriander, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 cinnamon stick, 6 cracked cardamom pods, 2 pierced dried limes, 2 chopped tomatoes, 1 tbsp tomato paste and 1.5 tsp salt. Add 1.5 litres water, cover and simmer for 75 minutes until the lamb is tender. Lift out the lamb and keep warm. Measure 750ml of the broth back into the pot, add the drained rice, cover and cook on low for 20 minutes. Fry 1 sliced onion in 1 tbsp oil until deep brown, adding 50g slivered almonds and 50g sultanas at the end. Pile the rice on a platter with the lamb, onions, almonds, sultanas and coriander.

w.note: Crisp cardamom and saffron dumplings tossed in warm date syrup and toasted sesame
w.how: Soak a pinch of saffron threads in 2 tbsp warm milk for 5 minutes. Whisk 250g plain flour, 1 tbsp cornflour, 7g dried yeast, 1 tbsp caster sugar, 0.5 tsp ground cardamom and a pinch of salt with the saffron milk and 300ml warm water into a thick, smooth batter. Cover and leave for an hour until bubbly and doubled. Heat 1 litre vegetable oil to 175C and drop in small spoonfuls, turning, for 4 to 5 minutes until deep golden. Drain, toss with 125ml warm date syrup and scatter with 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds.

d.note: Gin shaken with fresh mango, lime and cardamom syrup, topped with soda over ice
d.how: Simmer 60g caster sugar with 60ml water and 4 crushed cardamom pods until dissolved, then cool and strain. Blend the flesh of 1 large mango until smooth. Shake 240ml gin with the mango, the juice of 2 limes and the syrup with ice, in two batches. Strain into 4 tall glasses of ice, top with 400ml chilled soda water and garnish with lime wheels.
